sections.title: Purpose and Scope
paragraphs: The purpose of this policy is to implement the process followed for associate disciplinary action at Cotelligent. This policy covers Misconduct, Conduct of Enquiry, Punishments, Suspension and Suspension Allowance during disciplinary proceedings, and Grant of Service Letter and Payslips.

All associates of Cotelligent are subject to this Disciplinary Action Policy. Non-compliance with company policies, procedures, and standards of conduct may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

sections.title: Misconduct — Prohibited Behaviours
paragraphs: Associates of Cotelligent are prohibited from committing misconduct within the premises of Cotelligent. Misconduct shall mean and include the following: Theft, fraud and dishonesty; Demand, offer and acceptance of bribes or illegal gratification; Smoking in office premises; Disorderly or indecent behaviour within office premises.

Additional acts of misconduct include: Taking photographs of any operation, machine or function, photocopying and taking out of the premises any drawings, sketches, or documents; Wilful insubordination or disobedience; Manhandling other associates or superiors; Sleeping on duty at the desk; Intentional disclosure of associate's or company's confidential data or policies and procedures.

Falsifying records or reports, including but not limited to employment applications, time sheets, sales records, personal expenses reports, service level or compliance-related reports, is also considered misconduct. Any act likely to harm or endanger the company's property, and refusal to be interrogated by any enquiry officer or to sign any statement recorded in accordance with applicable law or policy are also prohibited.

Further acts of misconduct include: Habitual late coming or frequent absenteeism, or absenteeism for more than 3 days at a stretch without proper intimation as per applicable policies; Refusal to work on another job of same status when directed by reporting manager; Gambling within the premises; Collection of money or distribution of leaflets or pasting notices in Cotelligent without written sanction from the competent authority.

Writing anonymous letters or otherwise criticizing Cotelligent or TechDemocracy to any outside agency; Habitual negligence resulting in errors in excess of permissible percentage; Frequently leaving office without requisite permission; Holding meetings in the premises not related to work without permission; Creating disturbances or agitation of any nature in the premises; Acting in a manner against an agreement or award under the Shops & Establishment Act.

Engaging or abetting in abuses and physical violence to any other associate; Taking part in or instigating a strike which is unlawful or illegal; Habitual breach of rules or instructions of any kind; Failure to observe safety instructions; Doing private work during official working hours of Cotelligent or TechDemocracy; Unauthorized possession of any lethal weapon; Engaging in any other gainful employment while absenting from duty; Obtaining leave by citing false reasons; Conviction for any criminal offence involving moral turpitude.

Sexual harassment of any associate at the workplace is strictly prohibited misconduct. Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexually determined behaviour such as: Physical contact and advances; Demand or request for sexual favours; Sexually coloured remarks; Showing any pornography; Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

sections.title: Conduct of Enquiry — Disciplinary Procedure
paragraphs: The following procedures shall ordinarily be followed to conduct a departmental enquiry for the purpose of verifying the accuracy of the allegation of misconduct and taking appropriate action.

(a) An Enquiry Committee is set up with 3 associates of Cotelligent — the Global Delivery Head, HR, and one associate elected by both the Delivery Head and HR. The authorised committee shall give a notice to the concerned associate clearly stating the misconduct and calling on him or her to provide a written explanation within a specified time period.
(b) The associate shall be given at least 2 days' time for submitting their explanation. This time may be extended for a maximum of 5 days as a grace period.

(c) If the associate fails to submit their explanation within the prescribed time, or if the explanation submitted is not satisfactory, the enquiry committee shall hold an enquiry and issue a notice containing the details of the incident, name of the enquiry officer, and the date, time, and place of enquiry. If the associate admits the charges in writing voluntarily, the enquiry committee may award punishment without holding a formal enquiry.

(d) During the enquiry, evidence produced by the employer against the associate is recorded first, and the accused associate shall be given an opportunity to cross-examine witnesses. The associate's own statement shall then be taken and they shall be given the opportunity to produce all evidence in their support. Defence witnesses may be cross-examined by the Management representative.

(e) On request by the associate, the enquiry officer shall issue a written requisition to the employer to produce any document or information relevant or necessary for the enquiry. The employer shall produce or furnish such information unless it is prejudicial to the interest of the establishment.
(f) The accused associate shall cite any associate of the establishment as a defence witness, and the enquiry officer shall call such witness to give evidence.
(g) At such an enquiry, the accused associate shall be entitled to be assisted by a co-worker.
(h) The enquiry officer shall, on conclusion of the enquiry, submit a written report giving findings with reasons to the authority which appointed the enquiry officer.
(i) The management shall impose punishment on the basis of the enquiry officer's report.
(j) The order of punishment shall be communicated to the accused associate along with a copy of the enquiry report.

sections.title: Punishments
paragraphs: In case the management is satisfied that any offence has been committed by the associate concerned, after following the procedure established in this document, it may determine that such associate shall be liable to be dismissed, or may impose a lesser punishment after taking into consideration the gravity of misconduct, all extenuating or aggravating circumstances, and the previous record of the associate.

Punishment may include one or more of the following: Discharge from service; Stoppage of increment(s) with or without cumulative effect; Demotion; Suspension without wages for a period up to 15 days; Making an adverse entry in the service record; Warning or Notice for violating disciplinary policy; Recovery of loss of goods expressly entrusted to the associate, or money for which the associate is accountable, or any other recurring loss caused as a result of commission of misconduct.

sections.title: Suspension and Suspension Allowance During Disciplinary Proceedings
paragraphs: Where a disciplinary proceeding against an associate is contemplated or is pending, or where a criminal proceeding against the associate in respect of any offence is under investigation or trial, and the employer is satisfied that it is necessary or desirable to place the associate under suspension, HR may issue an order in writing to suspend the associate with effect from such date as may be specified in the order.

An associate who is placed under suspension shall be paid a subsistence allowance during the period of suspension as follows: 50% of the Basic Salary for the first 90 days of suspension; 75% of the Basic Salary if the suspension is extended beyond 90 days; 100% of the Basic Salary if the suspension is extended beyond 180 days.

An associate under suspension shall not be eligible for any subsistence allowance if the suspension is extended beyond 90 days due to the associate not attending to or cooperating with the disciplinary proceedings in force.

sections.title: Issuing Service Letter and Pay Slips
paragraphs: Every associate who leaves employment, retires, is discharged, or whose services are otherwise terminated shall be given a service certificate and salary or pay slip on request in writing by the associate concerned.
Service letter and or pay slips during the service of an associate shall be granted, provided with mention of the reason for which it is issued.
